long_biography.plain_text:
Managing his family's soybean, corn and wheat farm introduced John W. Henry to commodity-price risk. He began hedging crops, then developed a rule-based system designed to follow trends without discretionary forecasts. That method became John W. Henry & Company, which managed institutional and individual capital across global futures, interest-rate and foreign-exchange markets.

Henry redirected the resulting wealth into sports. He assembled partners to acquire the Boston Red Sox and co-founded the company now known as Fenway Sports Group. As principal owner, he is the control person for FSG's clubs. The company, rather than Henry alone, controls the Red Sox and Liverpool Football Club. It also holds sports-media, motorsport, golf and real-estate interests. Separately, Henry owns and publishes The Boston Globe and co-founded iRacing.
